patterns.usage_note: Knocks down what the listener was assuming and puts the opposite, or something far more extreme, in its place. The second clause typically carries も, まで, or a negative to mark the size of the leap. It attaches straight to a bare noun with no particle, to the bare stem of a な-adjective (元気どころか、寝込んでいる), and to the plain form of verbs and い-adjectives. どころではない states that circumstances rule X out; どころか needs a second clause that overturns or outdoes X.

examples.ruby: 姉[あね]は英語[えいご]どころか、フランス語[ご]まで自由[じゆう]に話[はな]す。
examples.english: English is the least of it: my sister speaks fluent French too.

examples.ruby: 今月[こんげつ]は旅行[りょこう]どころか、外食[がいしょく]する余裕[よゆう]もない。
examples.english: Forget a trip this month, I can't even afford to eat out.

examples.ruby: この薬[くすり]は効[き]くどころか、かえって熱[ねつ]が上[あ]がった。
examples.english: Far from helping, this medicine actually pushed my fever higher.
